problem.title: The problem we solve
problem.lead: Given a single-channel (mono) recording with multiple overlapping sounds, estimate how many distinct sources are active, name what they are, and separate sparse speech into individual stems.

cards.title: Why count before separating?
cards.body: Most audio separators assume you already know how many speakers or instruments are talking at once (for example, fixed 2-speaker or 3-speaker models). In real rooms, the count changes from clip to clip. Counting first tells downstream tools whether separation is even feasible.

cards.title: Why mono audio is hard
cards.body: With two or more microphones you can use spatial direction-of-arrival. With a single channel, all sources sum into one pressure wave: overlapping harmonics, reverberation, and loudness differences mask quieter sounds as density grows.

cards.title: Where this matters
cards.body: Acoustic scene monitoring, meeting and classroom analytics, hearing-aid pre-processing, and dataset curation all need reliable source-density estimates before spending compute on separation or transcription.

data.title: The data
data.lead: EchoCount is trained and evaluated on deduplicated mixtures from the SANADA Combined Acoustic & Speech corpus plus an isolated FSD50K benchmark subset.
notes: SHA-256 deduplication: 198 within-folder duplicate mixtures and 1 entire duplicate folder (Org_Fsd_Mix / Org_Mix_4_Sounds_Variable) are excluded before splitting so identical waveforms never leak across train, val, and test.
Speaker-disjoint evaluation: 3 of the 13 speakers in the speech corpus are held out completely to measure generalization to unseen voices.
Taxonomy: 5 coarse acoustic groups (Human voice, Musical instrument, Animal, Household/tools, Environment/other), 32 fine FSD classes, and 527 AudioSet classes (559 recognised classes total).

pipeline.title: The full pipeline, step by step
pipeline.lead: Every uploaded clip passes through six deterministic stages on the server. No stage invents labels or stems when a model is missing or a quality gate fails.

steps.name: Decode & Window
steps.detail: Convert to mono at 16 kHz. Clips longer than 8 s are centre-cropped to 128,000 samples (8.0 s) for counting; shorter clips are zero-padded. Original sample rate is preserved for stem export.

steps.name: Log-Mel Spectrogram
steps.detail: STFT with 1,024-sample Hann window (64 ms), 256-sample hop (16 ms), and 64 mel bands (40 Hz–8 kHz), producing a 64 × 501 time-frequency grid (32,064 cells).

steps.name: Source Counting + MC-Dropout
steps.detail: SourceCountCNN (2–31) and a sparse specialist (2–8) run 30 stochastic MC-Dropout forward passes (p = 0.4), calibrated via isotonic regression fitted on validation data.

steps.name: 3-Stage Open-Vocabulary Tagging
steps.detail: GroupFineTaggerCNN scores 5 groups and 32 fine classes; AST scores 527 AudioSet classes; CLAP (HTSAT-Unfused) provides zero-shot audio-text matching and frame-level time ranges.

steps.name: Conditional Separation
steps.detail: Pure 2-speaker speech routes to pretrained SepFormer (WSJ0-2mix) + ECAPA-TDNN speaker verification. General mixtures only separate when a trained general checkpoint is active, plus a residual stem (mix − sum of stems).

steps.name: Three Quality Gates
steps.detail: Every separated stem is checked for near-copy correlation, energy conservation against the mixture, and self-consistency (re-tagging the isolated stem to confirm it still matches its label).

train.title: How we train
train.lead: Training uses the train and validation splits only; the test split is locked until final evaluation.
bullets: Dual-head objective: Smooth L1 regression loss + Cross-Entropy classification loss over integer counts, balancing exact classification with ordinal closeness.
Optimization: AdamW with CosineAnnealingLR, SpecAugment time/frequency masking, and class-balanced sampling so rare source counts are not drowned out.
Early stopping & calibration: Best checkpoint is selected by validation macro MAE. Isotonic calibration and sparse-specialist blending are fitted strictly on validation predictions—never on test.

evaluate.title: How we evaluate (the metrics, explained)
evaluate.lead: All numbers on this site are loaded directly from evaluation/public_summary.json, exported from real held-out test runs.

metrics.name: Exact Accuracy
metrics.meaning: Fraction of clips where the rounded integer count matches the exact ground-truth source count.

metrics.name: Within ±1 Accuracy
metrics.meaning: Fraction of clips within one source of truth—useful when dense mixtures overlap heavily.

metrics.name: MAE & Bias
metrics.formula: MAE = mean(|y_pred − y_true|), Bias = mean(y_pred − y_true)
metrics.meaning: Average absolute error in sources, and whether the model systematically under-counts (negative) or over-counts (positive).

metrics.name: Bootstrap 95% CI
metrics.meaning: Uncertainty interval around test metrics; bins with n < 30 are flagged unreliable.

metrics.name: Macro mAP & F1
metrics.meaning: Unweighted mean Average Precision across classes so frequent sounds cannot hide weak rare classes.

metrics.name: SI-SDRi (dB)
metrics.meaning: Scale-Invariant Signal-to-Distortion Ratio improvement in decibels over the unseparated mixture.

findings.title: What we found (honest results)
findings.lead: EchoCount works well on sparse mixtures of familiar voices and everyday sounds, and degrades measurably on dense overlaps and unseen speakers.

limits.title: Dense mixture saturation (K ≥ 9)
limits.body: Exact accuracy is strong at K=2 (77.8%), K=3 (73.0%), and K=6 (70.4%), then collapses to 0.0% at K=9 (bias −2.41 sources) as spectral overlap saturates the 64-band log-mel grid.

limits.title: Unseen-speaker generalization gap
limits.body: On the 3 held-out speakers (n=352), exact accuracy drops from 53.1% (overall speech) to 13.1% (MAE 2.05), showing the CNN partially memorizes training-set speaker timbres.

limits.title: General non-speech separation
limits.body: The synthetic query-separation benchmark averages +2.51 dB SI-SDRi across 16 classes, but only 39.3% of stems pass self-consistency re-tagging—so general separation is disabled in production unless a trained separator checkpoint is loaded.

keep_in_mind.title: Counting is not separating
keep_in_mind.body: Estimating K sources does not automatically produce K clean audio files. Real separation is currently enabled for 2-speaker speech via SepFormer WSJ0-2mix.

keep_in_mind.title: Long files are centre-cropped
keep_in_mind.body: Counting analyses the central 8 seconds (16 kHz mono). Shorter files are zero-padded. The Analyze waveform marks the exact analysed region.

keep_in_mind.title: Uncertainty is not accuracy
keep_in_mind.body: MC-Dropout spread and softmax confidence show model decisiveness, not ground-truth correctness—especially on unseen voices or dense scenes.

keep_in_mind.title: Automatic server cleanup
keep_in_mind.body: Uploaded audio, generated stems, and ZIP archives are stored in isolated job folders and deleted automatically after the configured TTL and on server startup.

reproducibility.title: Reproducibility
reproducibility.lead: Every number on this page can be reproduced from the repository CLI:
reproducibility.commands:
python scripts/download_models.py
python scripts/train.py all --full
python scripts/evaluate.py --export-public
python tests/golden_check.py --verify
python test_templates.py --full
